He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]] and was a [[2018 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2018 Consensus All-American]]. Bagley was selected with the second overall pick by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. At the end of the [[2018–19 NBA season|2018–19 season]], he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie First Team]]. After spending three and a half seasons with the Kings, he was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] at the 2022 trade deadline. He played for nearly three seasons with Detroit before being traded to the Wizards in 2024 and then traded again to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] during the 2025 trade deadline. ==High school career== Bagley attended [[Corona del Sol High School]] in [[Tempe, Arizona]], as a freshman, where he won the state championship and was named National Freshman Basketball Player of the Year by [[MaxPreps]].{{Cite web |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/263812/tempe-corona-del-sol-standout-marvin-bagley-iii-talks-scholarship-offers-family/ |title=Tempe Corona del Sol standout Marvin Bagley III talks scholarship offers, family |first=Arizona |last=Sports |date=June 6, 2015 |website=Arizona Sports}} His sophomore year, he transferred to Hillcrest Prep in [[Phoenix, Arizona]], where he was teammates with future #1 pick [[Deandre Ayton]].{{cite web|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2015/08/17/marvin-bagley-iii-leaving-corona-del-sol-join-hillcrest-hoops/31892649/|title=Marvin Bagley III leaving Corona del Sol to join Hillcrest Hoops|website=Azcentral.com}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2015/10/6/9467531/deandre-ayton-transfers-marvin-bagley-recruiting|title=DeAndre Ayton transfers to join Marvin Bagley III|first=Ricky|last=O'Donnell|date=October 6, 2015|website=SBNation.com}} He left Hillcrest Prep in November 2015. In January 2016, he enrolled in [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Chatsworth, California]].{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=January 2, 2016 |title=No. 1 sophomore Bagley enrolls at Sierra Canyon |url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/14487033 |access-date=January 17, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}{{cite web|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/01/27/marvin-bagley-iii-awaits-appeal-decision-cites-academics-transfer-reason/79400164/|title=Marvin Bagley III awaits appeal decision, cites academics as transfer reason|website=Azcentral.com}} He was ruled ineligible to play his first year at Sierra Canyon due to [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) rules.{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=January 20, 2016 |title=Bagley, No. 1 in 2018 class, ineligible this year |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/14612607 |access-date=January 17, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}{{cite web|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20161205/sierra-canyons-marvin-bagley-iii-ready-to-make-impact-on-basketball-landscape|title=Sierra Canyon's Marvin Bagley III ready to make impact on basketball landscape|date=December 6, 2016|website=Dailynews.com}} In his last season for Sierra Canyon, he averaged 24.9 [[points per game]] and 10.1 [[rebounds per game]]. He would be named for the All-[[USA Today]] First Team in 2017.{{Cite web |date=March 28, 2017 |title=2016–17 American Family Insurance ALL-USA Boys Basketball Teams |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/2016-17-american-family-insurance-all-usa-boys-basketball-teams |website=usatodayhss.com}} He would graduate a year early and [[reclassification (education)|reclassify]] into the 2017 class.{{Cite web |date=August 14, 2017 |title=Marvin Bagley III set to announce college and reclassification plans Monday |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/marvin-bagley-iii-set-to-decide-on-reclass-and-college-tonight-duke-usc-ucla-arizona |website=usatodayhss.com}} ===Recruiting=== Bagley was rated as a five-star recruit throughout his high school career and was formerly ranked as the top player in the 2018 class before his reclassification. Bagley played for WACG (We All Can Go), in the EYBL circuit, with known players such as Darius Garland and Tray Boyd III. During this time, Bagley and WACG were selected to play in the EYBL Peach Jam Tournament; Bagley picked up major awards and recognition with alongside help from Garland and Boyd III.{{cite web|url=http://www.scout.com/player/193060-marvin-bagley|title=Marvin Bagley, Duke Blue Devils, Power Forward|website=Scout.com}}{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/3389|title=Rivals.com|website=N.rivals.com}}{{cite web|url=http://www.masslive.com/hoophallclassic/index.ssf/2017/01/hoophall_classic_2017_prospect_7.html|title=Hoophall Classic 2017 Prospects: Marvin Bagley III is 2018's top overall prospect|website=Masslive.com|date=January 11, 2017 }}{{cite web|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article132600894.html|title=UK target Marvin Bagley proving he's best basketball recruit in 2018 class|website=Kentucky.com}} Bagley was ranked the No.1 overall recruit and No.1 power forward in the 2017 high school class.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/203733|title=Marvin Bagley III – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles|date=August 17, 2017|work=ESPN.com|access-date=August 17, 2017}} His first college basketball scholarship offer came from [[Northern Arizona University]] when he was 14.{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/recruiting/2013/07/03/14-year-old-phenom-marvin-bagley-iii-loaded-with-scholarship-offers/2478521/|title=14-year old phenom Marvin Bagley III loaded with scholarship offers|website=Usatoday.com}} Before beginning what would have been his senior year of high school, Bagley reclassified into the Class of 2017. On August 14, 2017, he announced that he successfully reclassified as a graduate from Sierra Canyon and was eligible to play college basketball for [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke University]] during the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]].{{Cite web |last=Biancardi |first=Paul |author-link=Paul Biancardi |date=August 14, 2017 |title=No.1 recruit Marvin Bagley III to reclassify to Class of '17, play at Duke |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/20345857 |access-date=August 14, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}} thus allowing him to enter the [[2018 NBA draft]] as an early entry in the collegiate level.{{cite web |last=Chavez |first=Chris |date=July 16, 2017 |title=Report: Top HS recruit Marvin Bagley considering In addition to that, Bagley joined [[Deandre Ayton]] and [[Trae Young]] as the most freshmen players to join the consensus All-American First Team in a season. Following Duke's loss in the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA men's basketball tournament]], Bagley announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{Cite news |date=March 28, 2018 |title=Freshman Marvin Bagley III leaving Duke for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22946809 |work=[[ESPN]]}} ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2018–2022)=== [[File:Bagley2019.jpeg|thumb|right|Bagley taking a free throw against the [[Los Angeles Lakers|Lakers]] in March 2019]] On June 21, 2018, Bagley was selected second overall in the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]], behind his former high school teammate [[Deandre Ayton]].{{cite web |date=June 21, 2018 |title=Kings go power forward route with Marvin Bagley III as No. 2 pick |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23867177 |access-date=June 27, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}} On July 1, 2018, he signed a rookie scale contract with the Kings.{{cite web |last=Whedbee |first=Alexander |date=July 1, 2018 |title=Kings Sign Marvin Bagley III |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-marvin-bagley-iii |access-date=July 2, 2018 |website=NBA.com}} Bagley made his professional debut with Sacramento on October 17, 2018, with 6 points and 5 rebounds in only 12 minutes coming off the bench in a 123–117 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz vs. Sacramento Kings – Box Score|url=https://www.nba.com/game/uta-vs-sac-0021800011/box-score|website=NBA.com|date=October 17, web|title=Sacramento Kings vs. New Orleans Pelicans – Box Score|url=https://www.nba.com/game/sac-vs-nop-0021800022/box-score|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2018|access-date=January 15, 2024}} On [[File:Marvin Bagley III (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Bagley with the Pistons in 2022]] On February 10, 2022, Bagley was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] as part of a four-team trade that sent [[Donte
